subject: Temporary recall/restore policy + backup escrow evidence request
messages:
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@brighthealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@brighthealth.com
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary recall/restore policy + backup escrow evidence request

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — BrightHealth is very interested in Redwood's Dedicated offering but our legal/ops teams need more detail before we can finalize the DPA annex. A few concrete asks from our side so we can close the procurement track: 

- Can you confirm whether Redwood supports a temporary recall (short-term restore) window for deleted customer data beyond the stated retention (e.g., a 30-day recall for lawful investigation)? If so, what authorizations and audit evidence are required?
- Where are backups stored (primary cloud regions and any cross‑region replication)? We preferentially need US-only storage.
- Does Redwood maintain a backup manifest or index we can reference for restore scopes? If yes, please provide a sample or schema.
- Are there any subprocessors involved in backup storage or restore workflows (names, regions, and subprocessor agreements)?
- For SOC 2 / evidence purposes: can you provide the minimal artifact set we can rely on to show a restore occurred (logs, restore ticket, MD5 manifest, snapshot id)?

I've attached an excerpt from our DPA with the language we'd like to map to your processes (dpa_snippet_v2.pdf). Can you respond with a summary and any artifacts you can share? If useful, feel free to loop in your compliance folks.

Appreciate it — goal is to have final signoff by next week.

Best,
Sara
Sara Bennett
Senior Procurement Manager, BrightHealth

[attachment: dpa_snippet_v2.pdf]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Team — forwarding BrightHealth's requests (below). They want concrete artifacts we can provide to map to their DPA excerpt. Short timeline (SIGNS next week).

Ask: can we produce a concise one-page summary + a sample backup_manifest.csv and a short checklist of the evidence we can provide for restores? Also confirm whether any non-US subprocessor touches the backup/restore path for this customer's intended US-only deployment.

Key items to include in summary:
- Temporary recall policy (who approves, TTL, audit trail)
- Backup locations and replication topology (region names, provider)
- Restore proof artifacts (ticket id format, audit logs, snapshot IDs, checksums)
- Subprocessor list limited to storage & tooling with links to subprocessor contracts

Kimberly — legal language on recall approvals and DPA mapping.
Karthik — ops: sample manifest + RTO/RPO and process for an ad‑hoc 30‑day recall.
Marissa — SOC2 evidence artifacts (what we can export quickly).

I'll consolidate and send to Sara.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Temporary recall/restore policy + backup escrow evidence request

Grace / team — quick operational dump below; attaching a sanitized sample manifest (backup_manifest.csv).

Summary:
- Backup topology: primary snapshots are taken hourly in us-east1 (GCP) with asynchronous cross‑region replication to us-west2 for geo redundancy. For customers who require US-only storage we can disable cross‑region replication on the per‑tenant config (BrightHealth is eligible).
- Temporary recall: we support an ad‑hoc restore window for soft‑deletes up to 30 days from deletion if the customer requests it. Restores are initiated by an ops runbook and require a written request from the contract owner + approval from Security (Grace) or Legal (Kimberly). Approval flow is logged in Jira ticket (format RBW-<numeric>).
- RTO/RPO: typical RTO for a single-tenant restore using snapshot retention is 4–6 hours; RPO is <1 hour for primary snapshots.
- Restore evidence: we can provide the following artifacts after a restore completes: (1) Jira ticket id and description, (2) snapshot id and manifest rows (filename, shard id, md5), (3) restore runbook execution log (ops user and timestamp), (4) storage provider operation id (GCP operation name). These are exportable as CSV/PDF.
- Subprocessors: storage is managed by Google Cloud Platform (GCP) US regions; we use a managed snapshot service (vendor: HelixStore Inc.) for snapshot lifecycle management — HelixStore has a processing agreement; no offshore subprocessors touch backup data for US-only configs.

Attached: backup_manifest.csv (sanitized sample with columns: snapshot_id, region, shard_id, file_name, md5, created_at)

If Legal or Security require a signed escrow or additional attestations we can escalate to the platform team; otherwise the above is what we can ship quickly.

- Karthik
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

[attachment: backup_manifest.csv]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@brighthealth.com>
Cc: contracts@brighthealth.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary recall/restore policy + backup escrow evidence request

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a consolidated response mapped to the DPA excerpt you sent. We can follow up with a short call if you want to walk through artifacts.

1) Temporary recall / short-term restore
- We support a 30‑day ad‑hoc restore (soft‑delete recall) for Dedicated customers.
- Authorization: written request from the customer’s contract owner + approval from Redwood Security or Legal. Approvals are captured in Jira (RBW-<id>) and preserved in our audit trail.
- Evidence provided post‑restore: Jira ticket id, snapshot ids, manifest lines (file names + md5), restore execution log, and storage provider operation id.

2) Backup storage and regions
- Primary snapshots in us‑east1 (GCP). Cross‑region replication is configurable; for BrightHealth we will disable automatic cross‑region copy to keep data in US-only regions.

3) Sample manifest + artifacts
- Attached is a sanitized backup_manifest.csv as an example of the manifest schema we publish.
- For SOC2 evidence we can export the restore log and manifest csv as signed PDFs and provide operation ids that map back to GCP. Marissa can provide the exact export format.

4) Subprocessors
- HelixStore Inc. (snapshot lifecycle manager) — US-only processes for US-only deployments.
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP) — storage provider; data residency follows region config.

5) Next steps & ask from you
- Please confirm: (a) BrightHealth requires US-only storage (we've assumed yes), (b) you accept Jira ticket id + artifact set as sufficient evidence for restore events, and (c) confirm DPA clause numbering to attach our summary.
- If you need a signed escrow arrangement or additional attestations, we can open that thread with Legal; that will add ~1 week.

I'll attach the manifest and the DPA mapping doc in a follow-up if you confirm. If all good, I can push a short amendment to the DPA mapping for signatures.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[attachment: backup_manifest.csv]
